sources.author: Jean Paques
sources.credit: YouTube : Hot Piano by J. Paques (1928) – View/save archived versions on archive.org Many thanks to Mitchy for finding this great novelty piece. I have posted the copy of the original score at this link: https://mega.nz/file/SYRyQTxS#VbTnR--7aeInSyKr4vj5XY96Nk_oHbgRbosqQRutST8 Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/22695868?from=youtube_share
sources.source_text: A great novelty piece from Europe by Belgian composer-pianist Jean Paques (1901-1974), one of a number of novelty scores he wrote. He also recorded it on Edison Bell Radio Records (No. 804). Thus began a long career as a recording artist, stretching into the 1950s, featuring novelty, jazz and easy listening tracks, a total of nearly 40 albums. He later moved to London and was known internationally under the name Jean Easter.

sources.title: File:NASA Uses Wind Tunnel to Test Advanced Air Mobility Aircraft Wing (LRC 2025 B714 V RVLT Project 14x22 Wind Tunnel Tiltwing Test Video for Public Affairs V0002068).webm
sources.author: NASA Langley Research Center
sources.credit: This image or video was catalogued by Langley Research Center of the United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) under Photo ID: LRC_2025_B714_V_RVLT_Project_14x22_Wind_Tunnel_Tiltwing_Test_Video_for_Public_Affairs_V0002068 .
sources.source_text: In May and June, NASA researchers tested a 7-foot wing model with multiple propellers in the 14-by-22-Foot Subsonic Wind Tunnel at NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia. The model is a “semispan” wing, or the right half of a complete wing. The wing is a scaled model of a design used in a type of aircraft called a “tiltwing.” A tiltwing aircraft combines features of both helicopters and fixed-wing airplanes. Several air taxi companies are building tiltwing designs, but what is learned from this research will impact nearly all types of advanced air mobility aircraft designs.

sources.source_text: Preparation and first takeoff the Antonov AN-22 "Antei" in the new livery. The Antonov An-22 "Antei" is a heavy military transport aircraft designed by the Antonov Design Bureau in the Soviet Union. Powered by four turboprop engines each driving a pair of contra-rotating propellers, the design was the first Soviet wide-body aircraft and remains the world's largest turboprop-powered aircraft to date. The An-22 first appeared publicly outside the Soviet Union at the 1965 Paris Air Show. Since then, the model has seen extensive use in major military and humanitarian airlifts.
